bandReport.notes:
ITEM 80 IS PRESENT AND COMPLETE — stem plus all four options, the last ending '(d) Cannot be determined as data is inadequate'. p42 (printed 43) is the last content page and the paper ends there; nothing is cut off. Item 57 is likewise whole: p34-c1 opens on the '57.' number itself with nothing above it.

BAND SEAMS. I verified the leading edge against p32 (printed 33, band b4's territory, NOT mine — read for structure only, not transcribed): it ends with item 56 complete through its option '(d) 8', and the last passage-based item there is 53, whose options close in p32-c1. So no directions block and no item is in progress across the p32/p34 seam, and item 57 — a standalone work-and-time problem making no reference to any passage — needs no external context.

TWO DIRECTIONS BLOCKS, each self-contained inside my band, so no passage had to be fetched from outside it.
(a) p36 (printed 37): 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items ... Read the following two passages'. Passage-1 (the opinions/accumulating-money passage) governs items 61 AND 62 — both sit directly under it and both say 'the passage'. Passage-2 (the two-sentence social-order quotation) governs item 63 alone, whose stem says 'With reference to the above passage'. 3 items total, matching the preamble's count.
(b) p40 (printed 41): a SECOND 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items ... two passages' block. Passage-1 (university research) governs items 71 AND 72; Passage-2 (floods and droughts) governs item 73 alone. Again 3 items, matching.
Items 64 and 74-80 are standalone and carry no context; item 64 sits after the p36 block's last item and is plainly independent (an election-percentage problem).

PASSAGE NUMBERING RESTARTS between the two blocks, so a reader scanning context strings alone will see two 'Passage-1' and two 'Passage-2'. Their prose is entirely different, so the four contexts do not collide on any hash.

LONELY CONTEXTS EXPECTED (2): items 63 and 73 each own their passage exclusively. These are the LEGITIMATE case findLonelyContexts names — a directions block carrying several passages gives one of them to a single item. No sibling lost a copy at a band seam. Items 61/62 and 71/72 correctly share one context each.

The 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items' preamble and the 'Passage-1' / 'Passage-2' labels are deliberately NOT included in any context field; contexts hold passage prose only. No per-item material was parked in context — every item's own statement list, code line and question text is in its stem. There are no data-sufficiency items in this band.

COLUMN CROPS: all ten column images (p34/36/38/40/42 x c1/c2) are clean. No line was sliced down its middle, no item number was missing from the top of a c2 crop, and no fragment of the neighbouring column bled in. Each c2 crop opened on a complete item number or a complete 'Passage-2' heading. I did not need to fall back to any pNN.png to read text; the full-page images were used for structure only, as instructed.

TYPOGRAPHY, transcribed as printed rather than normalised: the booklet sets the DECIMAL POINT as a raised middle dot in the UPSC house style. This appears in item 80's options ('40·5 kg', '40·8 kg') and in item 79's stem ('0·XY'). These are decimal points, NOT multiplication signs. Item 79's is inside a math zone as \(0 \cdot XY\); item 80's options are plain text carrying the literal · character. Flagged here so a later reader does not 'correct' them into products.

SCAN SPECKS, ignored as artefacts and not transcribed: a stray mark before '5000' in item 64 option (d), one between 'possibility' and 'is' in item 78 option (d), and one between 'annual' and 'precipitation' in the p40 Passage-2 prose. Each is a speck on a ~150 DPI scan, not printed punctuation.

DIGITS READ WITH EXTRA CARE and re-checked against the column crops at full size: item 58 '1261' and the nine-factor product 91-99; item 65's options 1063/1073/1083/1183 and its divisor list 6, 9, 12, 15, 18; item 66's '2430'; item 68's times 3:16/3:17 and 4:58/4:59; item 70's angles 90/50/45/75 and its four fractions 112/9, 125/6, 155/9, 250/9; item 74's '15 x 14 x 13'; item 75's sequence 2, 12, 36, 80, 150; item 76's options 105/525/945/1050; item 77's 9 cups, 6 coffee, 3 tea. No digit was genuinely ambiguous — nothing here required a guess.

No defective or duplicated options anywhere in the band; every item has four distinct alternatives. No number skips: 57 through 80 run consecutively with each appearing exactly once.

questions.context: To encourage research is one of the functions of a university. Contemporary universities have encouraged research, not only in those cases where research is necessary, but on all sorts of entirely unprofitable subjects as well. Scientific research is probably never completely valueless. However silly and insignificant it may seem, however mechanical and unintelligent the labours of the researchers, there is always a chance that the results may be of value to the investigator of talent, who can use the facts collected for him by uninspired but industrious researchers as the basis of some fruitful generalization. But where research is not original, but consists in the mere rearrangement of existing materials, where its object is not scientific but literary or historical, then there is a risk of the whole business becoming merely futile.
questions.stem: The author's assumption about scientific research is that

options.label: C
options.text: it is never without some value
